w:r.w:t: Frontend Visual Language & Component Specification | v1.0
Authoritative reference for all frontend component styling, layout, spacing, colour usage, and interaction patterns. Agents must apply this document when building or modifying any frontend code.

Visual design guidance in UI Spec documents (UI_Admin, UI_Manager, UI_Auditor, UI_Client). Those documents remain authoritative for screen layout and component behaviour. This document is authoritative for all visual styling.
React 18 + TypeScript + Shadcn/ui + Tailwind CSS + lucide-react
Supported via Tailwind dark: prefix. All tokens have dark equivalents defined in §3.
Sovereign Audit AI follows a modern light-canvas SaaS design language. The core principles are:
Light and airy — the page canvas is warm off-white (#f2f0ee). Cards float on it using shadow, not border.
Rounded and soft — everything from cards to buttons to inputs uses generous border-radius. Hard rectangular edges are eliminated.
Colour as accent, not structure — the brand purple palette is used for active states, highlights, and key actions. It is not used as heavy fills on structural chrome like sidebars.
Information density is controlled — tables and lists have room to breathe. Alternating row shading is replaced by hover states only.
Hierarchy through typography and weight — section headings rely on size and weight, not background fills or underline borders.
Agent instruction: When implementing any component not explicitly described in this document, default to the principles above. Prefer rounded, prefer light fills, prefer shadow over border.
These six colours are the complete brand palette. No other colours should be introduced.
bg-primary / text-primary / border-primary. Primary action buttons, active nav items, heading accents, link text.
bg-dark / text-dark. Dark sidebar text (light mode), H1/H2 text colour, modal headers, the deepest text on the platform.
bg-accent / text-accent. Progress bars, active tab indicators, badge highlights, focus rings, gradient endpoints.
bg-warm. Page canvas background (light mode). Also used as active nav item pill fill, table row hover, and secondary button background.
bg-mid. Divider lines, table column headers in non-primary tables, input placeholder backgrounds, tag/chip default fill.
bg-muted. Disabled state backgrounds, skeleton loader fill, inactive icon colour, secondary badge fills.
Apply these rules consistently across every component. Deviations require explicit justification.
Primary (#4f2d7f) is never used as a large fill
Only use primary as a fill on small elements: buttons, active nav pills, badge backgrounds, icon colours. Never fill an entire sidebar, header bar, or card with primary.
Dark (#2b144d) is text and deep surface only
Use dark for headings, the user card gradient on the sidebar, and modal/drawer headers. Not for background panels or page sections.
Use accent for focus rings, gradient-border elements, progress bar fills, and the coloured left-border on active sidebar items. Do not use as a button fill.
The page background is always warm white in light mode. Cards sit on top of it as white (#FFFFFF) surfaces elevated by shadow.
Mid Beige (#e0dcd7) is structure and separation
Use for horizontal dividers, table grid lines, and the sidebar's right-edge shadow baseline. Not for text or icon colours.
Muted Stone (#ccc4bd) is disabled and inactive
Inactive nav icons, disabled button text, skeleton loaders, placeholder text. Never use for active or actionable elements.
Status colours are strictly tint-based — never filled. Each status has a background tint and a text colour. These are additions to the brand palette, used exclusively for status communication.

Dark mode is activated by adding the class 'dark' to the <html> element. All Tailwind dark: variants use these overrides. Store the preference in localStorage under the key 'theme'.

Font family: Inter (primary). Fallback: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif. Load via Google Fonts or bundle with the app. Tailwind font-family config: fontFamily: { sans: ['Inter', 'system-ui', 'sans-serif'] }.

These are explicit instructions for the Antigravity agent when implementing or modifying the frontend using this design system.
Before writing any frontend component, check this document for the exact class specification. Do not improvise border-radius, shadow, or colour values.
Never use hard-coded hex values in JSX or TSX. Always use Tailwind tokens defined in tailwind.config.ts. If a colour is not in the config, add it to the config first.
Never use rounded-none or the default Tailwind rounded (4px) on any visible surface. Minimum radius: rounded-sm (6px).
Never use alternating row shading on tables. Apply hover state only (hover:bg-[#faf9f8]).
The sidebar background is bg-white in light mode. It is NOT bg-primary, bg-dark, or any purple fill.
All buttons are rounded-full (pill). No rectangular buttons anywhere on the platform.
Cards have no visible border by default. shadow-card replaces the border. Only exception: alert cards which have a left border accent.
Status badges are light tint + matching text (§7.5). Never filled with a solid colour.
All tabs use the pill style from §7.6. No underline tabs anywhere on the platform.
For every list, table, and board column: implement the empty state per §8.4 before moving on.
Implement all transitions per §8.1. Every interactive element must have a hover and focus state.
The user card at the bottom of the sidebar (§7.1.1) must use the gradient banner — this is a key brand moment.
Every Kanban audit card must include the Audit ID chip in mono style at the top. Generate the ID from the audit's uuid — use the last 6 characters, prefixed with 'AUD-'.
Dark mode must be implemented for every component. Test both modes before marking a component done.
Load the Inter font from Google Fonts by adding the @import to globals.css. Set it as the default sans font in tailwind.config.ts.
